Function to calculate static spawning potential ratio

Source: R/staticSPR.R
static_spr.Rd

An INTERNAL function used by yprBH_MinLL and yprBH_SlotLL to calculate static spawning potential ratio with the yield-per-recruit model

Usage

static_spr(
  tmax,
  ageInterval,
  Linf,
  K,
  t0,
  FLR,
  FLRint,
  FLRslope,
  MatAge,
  percF,
  percFSpawn,
  L,
  cm,
  cf
)

Arguments

tmax

A single numeric that represents the maximum age of fish.

ageInterval

A single numeric that represents the interval of ages to be used (e.g., 0.1 means that ages will be modeled by tenths of a year).

Linf

A single numeric that represents the point estimate of asymptotic mean length from the von Bertalanffy growth model OR an nls object created from fitting the von Bertalanffy equation to length-at-age data.

K

A single numeric that represents the point estimate of the Brody growth coefficient from the von Bertalanffy growth model.

t0

A single numeric that represents the point estimate of the x-intercept (i.e., theoretical age at a mean length of 0) from the von Bertalanffy growth model.

FLR

A single character to indicate the fecundity-length relationship; either "linear" or "log10".

FLRint

A single numeric that represents the intercept of the fecundity-length relationship.

FLRslope

A single numeric that represents the slope of the fecundity-length relationship.

MatAge

A single integer that represents the age at maturity.

percF

A numeric vector representing the percentage of females at each age, starting at age-1.

percFSpawn

A numeric vector representing the percentage of spawning females at each age, starting at age-1.

L

A numeric vector of lengths where mortality may change. Will assume first value is 0 if not provided. See details and examples.

cm

A numeric that represents natural mortalities for the length intervals in L. See details and examples.

cf

A numeric that represents fishing mortalities for the length intervals in L. See details and examples.

Value

A list of six elements

  • Regs is a list containing management regulations:

    • L = either minimum length limit or slot limit lengths.

    • M = natural mortality.

    • F = fishing mortality.

  • intcalcs is a data frame containing values used in calculating SPR.

    • t is the time step in years based on the ageInterval used.

    • L_t is the Length at time t.

    • Fec_t is the fecundity at time t.

    • percF_t is the percentage of females as specified in the input parameters.

    • percFSpawn_t is the percentage of spawning females as specified in the input parameters.

    • E_t = Fec_t x percF_t x percFSpawn_t

    • F_t is the instantaneous fishing mortality at time t

    • M_t is the instantaneous natural mortality at time t

    • Z_t is the total instantaneous mortality at time t

    • S_noexp_t is total annual survival with no exploitation at time t

    • S_exp_t is the total annual survival with exploitation at time t

    • S_noexp_t1 is the cumulative product of total annual survival with no exploitation up to time t

    • S_exp_t1 is the cumulative product of total annual survival with exploitation up to time t

    • P_noexp_t is the spawning potential with no exploitation at time t

    • P_exp_t is the spawning potential with exploitation at time t

  • P_unfished is the total spawning potential with NO exploitation.

  • P_fished is the total spawning potential with exploitation.

  • SPR is the spawning potential ratio based on specified regulations.

  • Num_Eggs is the total number of eggs expected based on specified regulations

Note that P_fished, P_unfished and SPR are set to 0 when they calculation yields a number less than 0.0001.

Details

This function is generally not used independently. It is called when requesting the spawning potential ratio while calculating yield-per-recruit.

Author

Derek Ogle, jason.doll@fmarion.edu

Examples

#===== Spawning potential ratio for fixed parameters with a single minimum length limit
#----- FAMS inputs
cf <- 0.1
cm <- 0.18
percF <- c(0,0,0,rep(0.50,27))
percFSpawn <- c(0,0,0,0.24,0.24,0.53,rep(1.00,24))
L <- 280    # MLL

# Adjust ageInterval to test effect of fine-tuning ages on estimates
spr_1a <- static_spr(tmax = 30, ageInterval=0.1,
                     Linf = 1349.5, K = 0.111, t0 = 0.065,
                     FLR = "linear", FLRint = -1057029, FLRslope = 2777.08,
                     MatAge = 4, percF = percF, percFSpawn = percFSpawn,
                     L = L, cm = cm, cf = cf)


#===== spawning potential ratio for fixed parameters with a slot limit
L <- c(200,300,400)  ## Recruitment L, then lower & upper L for harvest slot
cf <- c(0,0.25,0.60,0.15)
cm <- rep(0.30,length(cf))

spr_2a <- static_spr(tmax = 30, ageInterval=0.1,
                     Linf = 1349.5, K = 0.111, t0 = 0.065,
                     FLR = "linear", FLRint = -1057029, FLRslope = 2777.08,
                     MatAge = 4, percF = c(0,0,0,rep(0.50,27)),
                     percFSpawn = c(0,0,0,0.24,0.24,0.53,rep(1.00,24)),
                     L = L, cm= cm, cf = cf)
